replacements.before: These tipping points loom regardless of U.S. policy. Even if Washington had remained aggressive on climate action, the inertia in the earth system means some further warming is already baked in.
replacements.after: These tipping points loom regardless of U.S. policy. Even if Washington had remained aggressive on climate action, continued global emissions mean further warming remains likely.

replacements.before: The IPCC notes that due to thermal inertia, we're locked into at least some additional warming over the next decade "even if we were to reach net-zero emissions tomorrow".
replacements.after: The IPCC finds that [sustained net-zero CO₂, together with strong reductions in other greenhouse gases, can stabilize warming](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg3/chapter/chapter-3/).

replacements.before: In other words, stopping on a dime is not possible. The climate system has momentum, and the brakes only do so much. Add the fact that global emissions have continued to climb, and it becomes clear that surpassing critical thresholds is increasingly likely.
replacements.after: Reaching that point requires global emissions cuts. Add the fact that global emissions have continued to climb, and it becomes clear that surpassing critical thresholds is increasingly likely.

replacements.after: Recent events in California provided a cautionary tale. In August 2022, days after [California approved its 2035 new-car emissions rule](https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/news/california-moves-accelerate-100-new-zero-emission-vehicle-sales-2035),

replacements.before: California's grid operators begged EV owners not to charge their cars during a heatwave (to avoid blackouts). The state's grid, strained by air conditioning demand and reduced power supply, could barely support the existing number of EVs, let alone the millions more that policy would require. This incident, essentially telling drivers "please don't charge your mandated electric cars!", was a poignant reminder that infrastructure can be a limiting factor.
replacements.after: California's grid operator [urged EV owners to avoid charging from 4 to 9 p.m. during a heatwave, and to charge before 4 p.m. instead](https://www.caiso.com/Documents/california-iso-issues-flex-alert-for-today-aug-31.pdf). The grid was strained by air conditioning demand and tightening power supplies; the alert did not establish that existing EV numbers exceeded its capacity. This incident was a poignant reminder that infrastructure can be a limiting factor.

replacements.before: Now they plan to build a larger 10 MW demonstration thorium reactor in the Gobi Desert by 2030.

Molten salt reactors (MSRs) are an advanced concept where the nuclear fuel is dissolved in a hot salt liquid that circulates as both fuel and coolant. They have inherent safety advantages (if the reactor overheats, the salt can drain into a passive storage tank and solidify, stopping the reaction).
replacements.after: Some molten salt reactor (MSR) designs [dissolve nuclear fuel in a hot salt liquid that circulates as both fuel and coolant](https://www.ornl.gov/publication/liquid-fuel-molten-salt-reactors-thorium-utilization). Some designs include [drain tanks that keep fuel subcritical and remove decay heat](https://info.ornl.gov/sites/publications/Files/Pub197043.pdf).

replacements.before: Others are walk-away safe, meaning even in total loss of power they won't meltdown, a far cry from Chernobyl or Fukushima scenarios.
replacements.after: Others use passive safety systems designed to maintain cooling during a loss of power.

replacements.before: Gates's Natrium, for instance, and other small modular reactors are engineered to eliminate the potential for the kinds of failures that have haunted nuclear's reputation. And because they're smaller and often factory-produced, they promise lower costs and faster deployment.
replacements.after: [TerraPower says Natrium uses passive heat removal and a low-pressure cooling system to reduce accident risks](https://www.terrapower.com/faq/). And because they're smaller and often factory-produced, they promise lower costs and faster deployment.
